title: Rain-Proof Cooler Covers
description: Waterproof construction with sealed seams and drainage for evaporative cooler covers — keep cabinets dry in heavy rain and humid off-season storage.
benefits: Fully sealed seams on premium waterproof lines
Hydrophobic coating sheds wind-driven rain
Built-in drainage channels and grommets
Anti-mildew treated interior face
Rated for sustained heavy rainfall exposure

faqs.q: Will a rain-proof cover trap humidity inside?
faqs.a: Only if the unit is covered while wet inside. Drain, dry 24 hours, then install. Vented hems on some models allow slow breathability.

faqs.q: What waterproof rating do you target?
faqs.a: Premium PVC-backed lines target 5000 mm hydrostatic head. Specify your exposure class on the quote form.

faqs.q: Can rain-proof covers handle snow load?
faqs.a: They shed meltwater but are not insulated for freeze. Use winter or insulated covers where ice accumulation is heavy.

faqs.q: How do I clean a waterproof cover?
faqs.a: Wipe with mild soap and water; avoid petroleum solvents that attack PVC. Air-dry fully before folding.

sections.heading: Waterproof vs Water-Resistant
sections.body: Water-resistant 600D with PU coating beads light rain. Rain-proof packages add PVC or TPU lamination and seam sealing so standing water on a flat rooftop does not wick through stitching lines.
bullets: Water-resistant: off-season dust and light shower duty
Rain-proof: monsoon, coastal, and flat-roof pooling
See waterproof cooler covers category for SKU detail
Always drain the cooler before sealing under any cover

sections.heading: Construction Details
sections.body: Critical points are the top panel seam, corner gussets, and hem where water can channel inward. We position low-point grommets on large horizontal tops and reinforce around zippered access panels.
bullets: PVC-backed 300D or TPU-laminated 600D shell options
Double-stitched then sealed seam on premium tier
Split corners available for side electrical boxes
Compatible with ratchet tie-down without piercing sealed zones

sections.heading: Climate & Installation Notes
sections.body: Rain-proof covers are stiffer than oxford polyester. Allow the fabric to seat 48 hours after install and re-tension straps. In humid climates, dry the unit fully before cover-up to prevent mildew under the laminate.
bullets: Not a substitute for draining the reservoir
Pair with vented hem if condensation is observed
Inspect grommets annually for debris blockage
Rooftop installs: slope top toward drainage grommets

intro: Rain-proof covers go beyond water-resistant polyester: laminated barriers, taped or welded seams, and positioned drainage points keep water out of pad frames and motor wells during storms and wet winters.

title: UV Protection for Cooler Covers
description: UV-blocking fabrics and coatings for evaporative cooler covers — reduce fade, heat soak, and premature fabric failure on rooftop and sun-exposed units.
benefits: Blocks 99% of harmful UV rays on rated UPF 50+ fabrics
Prevents color fading and coating breakdown
Extends cover lifespan 2–3× vs untreated fabric
Reflective tops lower cabinet surface temperature
Available on 600D, 900D, and vinyl-backed bases

faqs.q: Is UV protection a spray-on or in the fabric?
faqs.a: It is built into the coating and yarn stabilizer package at manufacturing — not a field-applied spray that washes off.

faqs.q: Does a UV cover eliminate the need for a solid winter cover?
faqs.a: No. UV covers address sun; winter or insulated covers address freeze and snow. Many sites use different covers by season.

faqs.q: How do I verify UV rating on an order?
faqs.a: Request UPF documentation on the quote for commercial jobs. Standard UV-shield SKUs list UPF 50+ on the spec sheet.

faqs.q: Can I add UV coating to an existing cover?
faqs.a: We manufacture new covers to spec. Field recoating is not recommended — replace when the topcoat chalks.

sections.heading: How UV Damages Cooler Covers
sections.body: Ultraviolet light breaks polymer chains in polyester and vinyl, causing stiffness, cracking, and color shift. Horizontal top panels see the highest dose — especially on down-draft and rooftop installs with no shade.
bullets: South- and west-facing exposures degrade fastest
Dark colors absorb more heat than silver or white tops
Chalking on the fabric surface is an early replace indicator
Interior pads are not protected unless the cabinet shell is shielded

sections.heading: Our UV Protection Technology
sections.body: We specify UV stabilizers in the PU or TPU coating, UPF-rated yarns where required, and heat-reflective pigments on top panels. The UV-shield product line pairs 600D shell with a dedicated UV topcoat for full-roof exposure.
bullets: UPF 50+ options on select SKUs
Silver and white reflective tops for rooftop down-draft units
Fade-resistant stock colors: gray, charcoal, silver
Compatible with standard drawcord and strap hardware

sections.heading: When You Need UV-Rated Covers
sections.body: Specify UV protection for any cooler in direct sun more than 6 hours per day, coastal sites with reflected glare, or facilities that cannot replace covers every season.
bullets: Rooftop commercial and industrial cabinets
Southwest US, Australia, and Middle East installs
Property managers standardizing a fleet fabric spec
Pair with waterproof package only if rain exposure also applies

intro: Untreated polyester on a rooftop cooler can chalk and tear within two seasons in desert sun. UV protection combines stabilizers in the coating, fade-resistant dyes, and optional reflective top panels so the cover — and the cabinet beneath — sees less thermal stress.

title: Vented Cover Design
description: Vented and mesh-panel cooler covers balance debris protection with airflow — reduce condensation and mildew risk when solid covers would trap moisture.
benefits: Reduces condensation vs fully sealed covers
Maintains airflow through screened ports or mesh
Blocks debris and pests during mild seasons
Lowers mold and mildew risk in humid zones
Lightweight options for frequent on/off cycles

faqs.a: Screened vents may admit fine mist in driving rain. Use solid rain-proof covers during storm season; switch to vented when weather is dry.

faqs.q: Is vented the same as mesh?
faqs.a: Mesh covers are fully breathable. Vented solid covers use fabric panels plus discrete screened openings.

faqs.q: Can I add vents to a custom cover?
faqs.a: Yes. Mark desired vent locations on your order photos; we reinforce edges to prevent tear propagation.

faqs.q: Do vented covers help with smell or mildew?
faqs.a: Airflow reduces trapped moisture that feeds mildew on organic debris. The unit must still be dry inside before covering.

sections.heading: Vented vs Closed Covers
sections.body: Closed covers maximize rain and dust sealing. Vented covers trade some sealing for breathability — ideal when the unit is dry inside but ambient humidity would condense on a cold cabinet under plastic.
bullets: Closed: off-season, winter, heavy rain
Vented: mild climates, in-season debris duty
Mesh: maximum airflow, minimum rain protection
Hybrid: solid panels + screened vents on one face

sections.heading: Design Options
sections.body: We integrate mesh windows, louvered vents, and zippered mesh panels into otherwise solid 600D shells. Position vents away from prevailing rain when possible; underside vents suit wall-mount units.
bullets: Full mesh cover for in-season pest barrier
Partial vent band on solid winter cover hem
Custom placement from annotated photos
See mesh cooler covers for all-mesh SKU

sections.heading: Best Practices by Climate
sections.body: Humid coastal and Gulf climates benefit from vented or mesh strategies during shoulder seasons. Desert sites often use solid UV covers in summer storage and mesh only briefly during monsoon debris events.
bullets: Inspect vents for wasp nests each season
Clean mesh with hose — no machine wash
Do not combine vented cover with running cooler unless spec allows
Pair vented summer + solid winter for year-round programs

intro: Solid covers excel at sealing out winter weather; vented designs add screened ports or full mesh panels so air can move while leaves, birds, and insects stay out. The right choice depends on climate, season, and whether the unit is operating or idle.

title: Winter Protection for Cooler Covers
description: Insulated winter cooler covers protect evaporative units from freeze, ice, and snow during off-season shutdown — with thermal lining and weather-tight closures.
benefits: Insulated thermal barrier (foam or quilted lining)
Helps protect drained lines from wind chill
Snow-shedding top reduces load on flat cabinets
Tight-seal drawcord or zipper hem
Multi-layer shell for cold-climate storage

faqs.q: Is a winter cover the same as insulated?
faqs.a: Winter covers include insulation plus weather sealing for cold seasons. Insulated covers may be specified without full snow-shed top geometry.

faqs.q: Do I still need to drain the cooler?
faqs.a: Yes. Draining and drying are mandatory. The cover protects against exterior freeze and debris, not standing water inside.

faqs.q: Can I use a winter cover in a mild climate?
faqs.a: You can, but a lighter water-resistant cover may suffice. Winter SKUs are optimized for freeze and snow regions.

faqs.q: When should the winter cover come off?
faqs.a: Remove at spring commissioning before the first cooling run. Inspect pads and pan, then store the cover dry.

sections.heading: Why Winterize With a Cover
sections.body: Freeze damage often starts in residual moisture in the pan and distribution system. A winter cover does not replace draining — it adds a layer against ice, wind-blown snow, and debris after you complete shutdown procedures.
bullets: Blocks wind-driven snow into louvers
Reduces thermal shock on exterior panels
Keeps rodents and nesting debris out of the cabinet
Pairs with our winterizing guide checklist

sections.heading: Insulation & Fabric Options
sections.body: Winter SKUs bond 3–5 mm foam or quilted batting to a 600D shell. Outer face is water-resistant; inner face is treated against mildew. Extreme cold sites can specify thicker cores on custom orders.
bullets: Standard winter line: 600D + foam core
Upgrade to waterproof shell for wet snow regions
Charcoal and gray stocks; custom colors on volume
Heavier than summer covers — plan for two-person rooftop lift

sections.heading: Installation Checklist
sections.body: Shut down power, drain water, dry internals, then install the cover with all closures engaged. Route tie-downs so they do not compress insulation unevenly or tear corner stitching.
bullets: Never cover a running unit
Remove cover before spring startup inspection
Store folded loosely in summer — do not compress foam long term
See installation guide for rooftop strap routing

intro: Winter protection combines insulation, a snow-shedding top profile, and perimeter sealing to slow freeze-thaw damage on pads, float valves, and sheet-metal cabinets when the cooler is offline for months.
